clue.text: 22 in charge of sound

parts.note: the answer to 22 down means offspring, and a son is one

explanation.surface: An heir is put in charge of the sound system.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 refers to 22 down, ISSUE, meaning offspring, so it gives SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic is the adjective relating to sound waves, as in a sonic boom.

clue.text: Did well, so should be followed

explanation.surface: Someone who has done well deserves a following.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is one sense; the other is to come after someone, as an heir replaces a king.

clue.text: The prime minister had a point!

definitions.text: The prime minister had a point!

parts.words: The prime minister had a point!
parts.note: Lord ... was British prime minister in the 1770s, and the same name is one of the four points of the compass

explanation.definitionFit: Lord North led the British government during the American War of Independence; the word is also a compass direction.

clue.text: College friend seen about with a girl before tea

indicators.note: before puts the girl ahead of the tea in the answer

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
a lass is a girl
maté is a South American herbal tea

explanation.surface: A student is spotted out with a young woman before afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: MATE here is maté, the South American drink, not a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow student in the same class is a schoolmate or peer.

clue.text: A pointer's maybe given to sponsor

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A dog that points might be handed to a backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges all nine letters of A POINTERS, the S of the possessive included.
explanation.definitionFit: To patronise a business or artist is to support it as a backer.

clue.text: A man producing impressive results

parts.note: impressive is read literally: someone whose work is made by pressing ink onto paper

explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who prints makes impressions on paper with type.

clue.text: Hide here for treatment

parts.note: hide is an animal skin, not concealment, and treatment means curing it into leather

explanation.definitionFit: Skins are processed into leather at a works of this kind.

clue.text: No time to absorb quiet music

indicators.note: to absorb means to take something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: no looks like the figure zero, the letter O
an era is a period of time
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone too busy to take in some soft music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No time' gives O plus ERA, which absorbs P to make the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of staged drama set to music and sung throughout.

clue.text: One caring inordinately for greenness

indicators.note: inordinately means out of order, so the letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A person who cares excessively about the colour green, or the environment.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenness here is inexperience or naivety, a lack of knowledge.

clue.text: Outdoors

parts.note: read as two words, out doors: doors through which people leave

explanation.definitionFit: Ways out of a building are doors marked for leaving.

clue.text: Blooming motoring people!

parts.note: split as a land of drivers, a ..., and also a flower, hence blooming

explanation.definitionFit: A clove-scented garden flower; the clue also splits it into a nation of motorists.

clue.text: Boredom can make some children nuisances

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Tiresome children can drive a person to tedium.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'can make' into the definition; those words are a link, and 'Boredom' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness, the French word for tedium.

clue.text: Those constituents showing spirit

indicators.note: constituents are the parts that make up the word those, here put together again differently

explanation.surface: Voters in a constituency are showing great morale.
explanation.definitionFit: The characteristic spirit or values of a group or community.

clue.text: Consultation here could lead to an exchange of words

definitions.text: Consultation here could lead to an exchange of words

parts.words: Consultation here could lead to an exchange of words
parts.note: an exchange of words sounds like an argument, but it means swapping a word for a synonym found in a reference book

explanation.definitionFit: A reference book listing synonyms, used to swap one word for another.

clue.text: "Look on 'my works, ye Mighty, and - -!" (Shelley)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from the inscription in Shelley's sonnet Ozymandias

explanation.definitionFit: The missing final word of the inscription on the ruined statue in Shelley's Ozymandias, meaning lose all hope.

clue.text: Rushed around organising treat and made a splash

indicators.note: around says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: sped means rushed

indicators.note: organising means putting the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hurried about arranging a treat and caused a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rushed' looks like part of the definition but supplies the outer letters; 'organising' scrambles 'treat' and 'around' wraps the rushed word about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spattered means splashed, scattered drops over something.

clue.text: Told stories about the Orient and felt a longing for it

indicators.note: about says the stories wrap round the next piece

parts.note: to yarn is to tell tales
E, east, stands for the Orient

explanation.surface: A traveller spun tales about the East and grew homesick for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long or pine for something.

clue.text: Room at the top?

parts.note: room is read as space, and the top is the sky above, the zone of flight and rocketry

explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere and outer space, the domain of aviation and rocketry.

clue.text: The underworld bid for exoneration

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
to bid someone is to charge or command them

explanation.surface: A mobster makes an offer to be let off.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the classical underworld, Hades.
explanation.definitionFit: Release from a charge or duty, as when a court clears an accused person.

clue.text: They depict parts of the chest

explanation.surface: Artists paint pieces of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists who sketch are one sense; the sliding boxes of a chest of furniture are the other.

clue.text: Shows coldness is due to introduction of small fires

indicators.note: introduction of means just the opening letter of the word small is taken

parts.note: lights means sets fire to, ignites

explanation.surface: Someone acts frostily because a few little fires have been started.
explanation.definitionFit: Slights means snubs, treats someone with disdain.

clue.text: Generous donations secured with great craft

parts.note: large means great in size
SS, steamship, is a craft or vessel

explanation.surface: Lavish gifts obtained through great skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is generous giving of money or gifts to many.

clue.text: Support an associate — but only within the law

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
an ally is an associate or partner

explanation.surface: Back a colleague, provided it stays lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally means lawfully, in accordance with statute.

clue.text: The work of shop-assistants is telling

explanation.surface: A shop worker's job is quite revealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling goods to the public is one sense; recounting a story in detail is the other.

clue.text: Study English writer

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: Read a book by an English novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a nineteenth-century English novelist and dramatist.

clue.text: Offspring of 17

explanation.surface: The children of a particular person.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is 17 down, DISCHARGE: a flow of matter from a wound is also called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Children or descendants are one sense; an emission or discharge, as from a wound, is the other.

clue.text: Get out. of sight — the way remains to be found

parts.note: ST, street, is a way or road
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Something vanished from view, and the road's remnants are still undiscovered.
explanation.definitionFit: To stash is to hide or store away out of sight.

clue.text: Took head off herbaceous plant and found a snake

indicators.note: took head off means the first letter of the plant is removed

parts.note: madder is a herbaceous plant whose roots give a red dye

explanation.surface: A gardener beheaded a plant and discovered a serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake, a viper.

clue.text: Tapestry given 'retiring academician by others.

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
other members of the Royal Academy, more RAs

explanation.surface: A wall-hanging painted by an elderly Royal Academy member together with colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns RA into AR; the others are further academicians, RAS.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a wall-hanging woven with pictures, named after a French town.

clue.text: Call round accompanied by a foreigner

indicators.note: round says the call is placed about the next piece

parts.note: to holler is to shout or call
and means together with, accompanied by

explanation.surface: Ring someone who is travelling with an overseas visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Netherlands, a Dutch person, is foreign to a Briton.

clue.text: Finish in front of the French, astute as ever

indicators.note: in front of puts the finish ahead of what follows

parts.note: end means finish
les is French for the (plural)
sly means cunning, astute

explanation.surface: The French end up as shrewd as they always were.
explanation.definitionFit: Endlessly means forever, without stopping, as it always was.

clue.text: Just the home for young high fliers!

definitions.text: Just the home for young high fliers!

parts.words: Just the home for young high fliers!
parts.note: high fliers sounds like ambitious graduates, but means eagle chicks in their lofty nest

explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest built high on a crag, where its chicks are raised.
